title: Media Archive
manifesto: Coverage in leading media outlets serves as independent verification of the facts of persecution. When domestic justice demonstrates selective blindness, the role of the press in establishing the truth becomes decisive.

items.title: Six Months Without a Decision: Legal Vacuum in the Lagovsky Case
items.summary: RSE analyzes the situation regarding the delayed Ministry of Justice decision. The judicial stage is complete, but the final act remains unsigned, leaving the family in limbo.
items.focus: Serbia's political responsibility for surrender to a system lacking fair trial guarantees.

items.title: Court vs. Facts: Why is Serbia Ignoring Arbitration Rulings?
items.summary: An N1 report exposes a fundamental flaw in the process: Serbian justice refuses to consider exculpatory documents from the RF, focusing solely on Moscow's prosecutorial narrative.
items.focus: Violation of the principle of equality of arms and the right to defense.

items.title: Family at Risk: The Humanitarian Dimension of the Case
items.summary: Nova.rs on how a formal extradition procedure destroys children's lives and violates the right to family life (Article 8 ECHR).
items.focus: The priority of the children's best interests, disregarded by the court.

press_call.title: Media as a Safeguard
press_call.text: Systemic coverage in independent media confirms the existence of real risks. In international law, such publications are an important indicator in assessing the safety of extradition.
press_call.thesis: We are open to cooperation with journalists and provide access to all primary case documents.
